tasks.task:
## What
Add a `POST /health` endpoint that returns build metadata, with tests that drive real requests. Keep the change scoped to the endpoint.

## Why
Operators currently learn a deploy is unhealthy from user reports, because nothing exposes build metadata to poll.

## Acceptance criteria
- `POST /health` returns the build metadata contract, proven by tests that drive real requests.
- One failure path is proven alongside the happy path.
- Nothing outside the endpoint and its tests changes.
tasks.done_when: real requests prove the endpoint response and validation behavior, and the repository's full gate passes
tasks.title: feat(api): add /health endpoint

tasks.task:
## What
Document the new `/health` endpoint: its request, its response, and worked examples.

## Why
Operators are being asked to poll an endpoint that appears in no documentation, so each of them has to read the service source to learn its response shape.

## Acceptance criteria
- The request and response are documented with field names and types.
- Every example was run against the API and behaves as written.
- The documented contract matches the endpoint as implemented, not as proposed.
tasks.done_when: all task acceptance criteria are met and every documented example was verified against the running API
tasks.title: docs(api): document /health

tasks.task:
## What
Add a typed `health()` method to the client that calls `GET /health`, with a test against a real local server.

## Why
Every consumer of the new endpoint is otherwise left to hand-roll the request and its response type, which is where the contract drifts first.

## Acceptance criteria
- `health()` returns the build metadata as a declared type rather than an untyped mapping.
- A test drives it against a real local server rather than a mocked transport.
- One failure response is covered alongside the happy path.
tasks.done_when: all task acceptance criteria are met, the method is typed at its boundary, and the repository's full gate passes
tasks.title: feat(client): add health() method

steps.task:
## What
Implement a read-only `/admin` dashboard page that surfaces the health metadata, with tests that render the page and drive real requests.

## Why
Operators can poll the endpoint but have nowhere to see its metadata without a terminal, which is what keeps on-call reading raw JSON during an incident.

## Acceptance criteria
- The rendered dashboard exposes every field the health contract returns.
- Tests render the page and drive real requests rather than asserting on internal state.
- Access control is covered: an unauthorized viewer is refused, and a test proves it.
steps.done_when: the rendered dashboard exposes every health field through real requests, access control is covered, and the full gate passes

steps.task: Exercise the dashboard in staging and approve final review.
